scope: Plans only; no runtime success inferred.

A.evidence: "all requests remain within the permitted public boundary" and "readable report, nonzero failures"; it also requires bin/verify-web full to run the verifier against the local built server.
A.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

A.evidence: "Crawl `/` and `/sitemap.xml`"; it requires byte-identical sitemap, canonical, and internal-link values, rejects encoded slashes and non-root trailing slashes, and checks sitemap status, self-canonicality, and noindex.
A.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

A.evidence: It specifies homepage `/` versus `/home`, exactly one `/products/{slug}` 200 URL, `/shop/{id}` and digest collection redirects, and explicit 301/302 Location and cache-header checks.
A.omissions: The exact long-max-age threshold remains a stated prerequisite, correctly not invented.

A.evidence: It requires exactly one Product JSON-LD block matching visible values and the #35 feed, with an explicit scoped skip/expected failure before the prerequisite; it separately requires EmDash built-in provenance for robots.txt and sitemap.
A.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

A.evidence: "Separately authored public-route fixture with home, collection, and products" is a populated positive case; the independent manifest is not generated from the outputs under test. It lists broken links, loops, noncanonical variants, canonical conflicts, redirect/header errors, and structured-data mismatch, with expected failures and L/P/R evidence.
A.omissions: The plans are prospective and therefore contain no executed observation; this is appropriate for the task.

A.evidence: It names deterministic fixtures plus local built server, preview, and production ("L/P/R"), requires local-to-preview-to-production order, identifies origin/flag/result evidence, and says source proof cannot establish released or deployed readiness.
A.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

A.evidence: It keeps #34/#35 checks as explicit scoped skips/expected failures, identifies route/feed/demo/cache prerequisites, requires activation after landing, updates FEATURE_MAP, and preserves the supplied `/collections/{slug}` vocabulary and ownership boundaries.
A.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

A.evidence: It names `pnpm verify`, existing desktop/mobile and profile regressions, proof locations, exact source anchoring, and separately gated PR/deployment/merge actions without needless permission requests.
A.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

B.evidence: "Permit only GET/HEAD against public routes" and "exclude admin and mutation routes, including redirect destinations"; it requires origin, offending URL, chain, failure, and dependency-skip reporting plus nonzero failure status.
B.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

B.evidence: It crawls `/` and `/sitemap.xml`, follows public links and sitemap entries, rejects `%2F` and trailing-slash variants, preserves raw bytes, and requires 200/self-canonical/non-noindex sitemap pages.
B.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

B.evidence: It requires `/` only, excludes `/home`, requires one `/products/{slug}` 200 URL, checks both legacy route families, and checks 301/302 status, Location, immutable, and long max-age behavior.
B.omissions: The long-max-age threshold is correctly left to source/policy discovery rather than guessed.

B.evidence: It requires exactly one Product JSON-LD block matching page and #35 feed data, names dependency-specific skips with activation conditions, and requires public EmDash built-in ownership evidence for robots.txt and sitemap.
B.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

B.evidence: It promises "deterministic HTTP fixtures covering successful behavior and each failure class" and a local integration test, but does not explicitly define independently sourced expected facts or a known-good populated page/product case with an expected observation.
B.omissions: The plan never states that its success fixture is populated with actual pages/products, never identifies an independent oracle/manifest, and does not explicitly say what a capable populated integration surface must observe. A fixture generated from implementation output could therefore pass while sharing the same mistake.

B.evidence: It distinguishes deterministic fixtures, local built-server integration, and later preview/production origins; requires exact source, target, outcomes, skips, and reports; and states that read-only production verification neither deploys nor grants authority.
B.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

B.evidence: It names #34/#35 landing and contract discovery, dependency activation/removal of exemptions, FEATURE_MAP local-to-preview-to-production documentation, and preservation of product ownership and URL vocabulary.
B.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

B.evidence: It names `pnpm verify`, browser/profile regressions, source/outcome/skip recording, proof locations, and separate authorization for PR, deployment, publication, mutation, secrets, and merge.
B.omissions: No material omission against this criterion.

independent_expected_facts_oracle.basis: "independently specified fixture" and "independent product/collection identity-to-slug and legacy-path manifest"; it explicitly forbids deriving the comparison manifest from tested output.

known_good_populated_passing_case.basis: The plan explicitly names a populated fixture with home, collection, and products and expects permitted requests, valid routes, and a passing result on deterministic fixtures and L/P/R. This is prospective, not claimed execution.

independent_expected_facts_oracle.basis: It specifies checks and fixtures but does not say expected facts come from an independent source or prohibit deriving the oracle from the implementation/output.

known_good_populated_passing_case.basis: It mentions successful deterministic fixtures and local integration, but does not explicitly describe a known-good populated site with pages/products and an expected observation on that capable surface.

comparison.reason: A is hard-eligible and materially stronger on positive proof validity: it independently specifies expected facts and a populated passing case, while B leaves both properties implicit. A also explicitly guards against an oracle derived from sitemap/canonical/redirect/JSON-LD output. B is otherwise substantially complete and has no hard failure or material authority/environment regression, so the difference is a focused evidence-design advantage rather than a broad contract failure.

material_regressions.basis: Against A and the fixed positive-proof criterion, B omits an independent oracle and an explicit known-good populated passing observation. Its "successful behavior" fixtures could be empty, output-derived, or otherwise fail to prove the positive contract.

comparison.adoption_note: The verdict compares plans only and does not authorize implementation, promotion, deployment, publication, PR creation, or merge.
